==English==

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|sē|a=RP}}, {{IPA|en|/siː/}}
* {{audio|en|En-uk-to see.ogg|text=to see|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/si/|a=GA,CA}}
* {{audio|en|En-us-see.ogg|a=GA}}
* {{hmp|en|C|cee|sea|Seay|si}}
* {{rhymes|en|iː|s=1}}

===Etymology 1===
{{ety|en|id=perceive|:inh|enm:seen|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|seen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sēon||to see, look, behold, perceive, observe, discern, understand, know|id=see}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*sehwan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*sehwaną|t=to see}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*sekʷ-|t=to see, notice|id=see}}.

{{sno|en|refer to|pos=false|cap=1}} is a {{calque|en|la|vidē||see (thou)|pos={{2nd}} person singular imperative|nocap=1}}, which was also {{lg|borrowed}} into academic English (see {{l|en|vide|id=see consult}}) as well as {{l|pt|vide|Portuguese|id=see}}.

{{col-top|2|cog}}
Cognate with {{cog|sco|see}}, {{m|sco|sei|t=to see}}, {{cog|yol|sau}}, {{m|yol|ze}}, {{m|yol|zee}}, {{m|yol|zey}}, {{m|yol|zie|t=to see}}, {{cog|frr|se}}, {{m|frr|si}}, {{m|frr|siin}}, {{m|frr|siine}}, {{m|frr|siinj}}, {{m|frr|sä}}, {{m|frr|säie|t=to see}}, {{cog|stq|sjo|t=to see}}, {{cog|fy|sjen|t=to see}}, {{cog|bar|segn|t=to see}}, {{cog|gmw-cfr|sehn}}, {{m|gmw-cfr|senn|t=to see}}, {{cog|nl|zien|t=to see}}, {{cog|nds|sehn|t=to see; to look}}, {{cog|de|sehen|t=to see}}, {{cog|li|séëne}}, {{m|li|zeen|t=to see}}, {{cog|lb|gesinn|t=to see}}, {{cog|gsw|gseh|t=to see}}, {{cog|mhn|sechen|t=to see}}, {{cog|wym|zaon|t=to see}}, {{cog|yi|זען|t=to see}}, {{cog|da,nb,sv|se|t=to see}}, {{cog|ovd|sją̊|t=to see}}, {{cog|fo|síggja|t=to see}}, {{cog|is|sjá|t=to see}}, {{cog|nn|sjå|t=to see}}, {{m|sv|sia|t=to foretell}}, {{cog|got|𐍃𐌰𐌹𐍈𐌰𐌽|t=to see}}, and more distantly with {{cog|sq|shof}}, {{m|sq|shoh|t=to see}}, {{cog|la|secūtus}}, {{m|la|sequūtus|t=followed}}, {{cog|grc|ἕπομαι|t=to follow, obey}}, {{cog|fa|ا|tr=a}}, {{m|fa|از|tr=az}}, {{m|fa|ز|tr=ze|t=from, of}}, {{cog|xlu|𒁕𒀀𒌋𒄿𒅖|t=eye}}, {{cog|sa|सच्|t=to be associated with, familiar with, have to do with}}.
{{col-bottom}}

====Verb====
{{wikidata lexeme|L185}}
{{en-verb|+|+|saw,~n<l:dialectal>,~nt<l:dialectal>,~d<l:dialectal>|n,~nt<l:dialectal>,~d<l:dialectal>,saw<l:dialectal>,sawn#Etymology_2<l:dialectal or [[eye dialect]]>}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[perceive]] or [[detect]] someone or something with the [[eye]]s, or as if by [[sight]].
#* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|page=18|chapter=I|passage=Pretty soon I struck into a sort of path.{{...}}It twisted and turned,{{...}}and opened out into a big clear space like a lawn. And, back of the lawn, was a big, old-fashioned house, with piazzas stretching in front of it, and all blazing with lights. 'Twas the house I'd '''seen''' the roof of from the beach.}}
#* {{RQ:Heyer Unknown Ajax| chapter=1| passage=But Richmond{{...}}appeared to lose himself in his own reflections. Some pickled crab, which he had not touched, had been removed with a damson pie; and his sister '''saw'''{{...}}that he had eaten no more than a spoonful of that either.}}
## To [[witness]] or [[observe]] by personal [[experience]].
##: {{hyponyms|en|experience|suffer}}
##: {{ux|en|Now I've '''seen''' it all!}}
##: {{ux|en|I'm '''seeing''' much better since I got my eyeglasses recalibrated.}}
##: {{ux|en|I have been blind since birth and I love to read Braille. When the books arrive in from the library, I can’t wait to '''see''' what stories they have sent me.}}<!--illustrates that this def does not mean vision-->
##* {{RQ:King James Version|John|8|51|page=1330|column=1|passage=Uerely, verely I ſay vnto you, If a man keepe my ſaying, hee ſhall neuer '''ſee''' death.}}
##* {{RQ:Dickens Nicholas Nickleby|page=434|passage={{...}} And remember this, 'scape-gallows,' said Ralph, menacing him with his hand, 'that if we meet again, and you so much as notice me by one begging gesture, you shall '''see''' the inside of a jail once more {{...}}}}
## To watch (a movie) at a [[cinema]], or a [[show]] on [[television]] etc.
##: {{ux|en|I '''saw''' the latest Tarantino flick last week.}}
# To form a [[mental]] [[picture]] of, to [[perceive]] in a certain way.
#: {{ux|en|I '''see''' it as essential that there should be somewhere to park.}} 
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=14 October 2014|author=David Malcolm| page=173| title=The Great War Re-Remembered: Allohistory and Allohistorical Fiction| work=The Great War in Post-Memory Literature and Film| editors=Martin Löschnigg; Marzena Sokolowska-Paryz| url=https://books.google.co.nz/books?id=4Y_nBQAAQBAJ| publisher={{w|de Gruyter|Walter de Gruyter GmbH & Co KG.}}| isbn= 9783110363029| passage=The question of the plausibility of the counter-factual is '''seen''' as key in all three discussions of allohistorical fiction (as it is in Demandt's and Ferguson's examinations of allohistory) (cf. Rodiek 25–26; Ritter 15–16; Helbig 32).}}
#* {{RQ:Time|title=When Did On-Screen Weddings Get So Bleak?|date=May 27 2026|author=Judy Berman
|text=Cathy and Cassie '''see''' their husbands as their best chance at securing comfortable lives.
|url=https://time.com/article/2026/05/14/testaments-finale-red-wedding-season/
|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260528000830/https://time.com/article/2026/05/14/testaments-finale-red-wedding-season/}}
## {{lb|en|figuratively}} To [[understand]].
##: {{ux|en|Do you '''see''' what I mean?}}
##* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-06-28|author=w:Joris Luyendijk| volume=189| issue=3| page=21| magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly|url=http://www.guardian.co.uk/commentisfree/joris-luyendijk-banking-blog/2013/jun/19/banking-britain-beyond-control|title=Our banks are out of control| passage=Seeing the British establishment struggle with the financial sector is like watching an alcoholic{{...}}. Until 2008 there was denial over what finance had become.{{...}}But the scandals kept coming{{...}}. A broad section of the political class now recognises the need for change but remains unable to '''see''' the necessity of a fundamental overhaul.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261013062852/https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/joris-luyendijk-banking-blog/2013/jun/19/banking-britain-beyond-control|archivedate=13 October 2026}}
## {{lb|en|figuratively}} To come to a [[realization]] of having been mistaken or misled.
##: {{ux|en|They're blind to the damage they do, but someday they'll '''see'''.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[foresee]], [[predict]], or [[prophesy]].
##: {{ux|en|The oracle '''saw''' the destruction of the city.}}
##* {{quote-song|en|title={{w|Happy Together (song)|Happy Together}}|year=1967|artist=w:The Turtles|author={{w|Alan Gordon (songwriter)|Alan Gordon}}; Garry Bonner|text=I can't '''see''' me lovin' nobody but you / For all my life / When you're with me, baby the skies'll be blue / For all my life}}
## {{lb|en|used in the imperative}} {{n-g|Used to emphasise a proposition.}}
##: {{ux|en|You '''see''', Johnny, your Dad isn't your real father.}}
##: {{ux|en|You're not welcome here any more, '''see'''?}}
# {{lb|en|social}} To meet, to visit.
## To have an interview with; especially, to make a call upon; to visit.
##: {{ux|en|You'd better '''see''' about that with the boss.}}
##* {{RQ:King James Version|1 Samuel|15|35|page=386|column=2|passage=And Samuel came no more to '''ſee''' Saul vntill the day of his death: neuertheleſſe, Samuel mourned for Saul: and the {{smallcaps|Lord}} repented that he had made Saul king ouer Iſrael.}}
## {{senseid|en|to date}} To [[date]] frequently.
##: {{ux|en|I've been '''seeing''' her for two months.}}
## To visit for an appointment, especially a [[medical]] appointment.
##: {{ux|en|You should '''see''' a doctor about that rash on your arm.}}
##: {{ux|en|I've been '''seeing''' a therapist for three years now.}}
##: {{ux|en|I '''saw''' my parole officer this morning for a drug test.}}
## To be attended to during an appointment, especially a medical appointment.
##: {{ux|en|The doctor will '''see''' you now.}}
# To be the [[setting]] or [[time]] of.
#: {{ux|en|The 20th century '''saw''' humanity's first space exploration.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|author=David Sprague|title=Buffalo Tom Reaches Crossroads: EastWest Trio At Make-Or-Break Point| journal={{w|Billboard (magazine)|Billboard}}| date=1995-06-03| volume=107| issue=22| page={{gbooks|1gsEAAAAMBAJ|9|sees}}| passage=It seems as if every passing year '''sees''' the mainstream embrace a longtime cult-favorite alternative rock band.}}
# To be a [[group]] which contains a thing.
#: {{ux|en|This year's class '''saw''' many excellent pupils.}}
#: {{ux|en|The punk music genre '''saw''' a large number of new bands.}}
# {{lb|en|by extension}} {{n-g|Chiefly followed by '''''[[that#Conjunction|that]]'''''}}: to [[ensure#Verb|ensure]] that something happens, especially by personally [[witness#Verb|witnessing]] it.
#: {{ux|en|I'll '''see''' you hang for this}}
#: {{ux|en|I was at the docks '''seeing''' that the goods got properly unloaded.}}
#: {{ux|en|I '''saw''' that they didn't make any more trouble.}}
#* {{RQ:Blackstone Commentaries|book=I|chapter=Of Corporations|page=469|passage=As to eleemoſynary corporations, by the [[dotation#Noun|dotation]] the founder and his heirs are of common right the legal viſitors, to '''ſee''' that that property is rightly employed, which would otherwiſe have deſcended to the viſitor himſelf: {{...}}}}
#* {{RQ:G&M|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20221217203636/https://www.theglobeandmail.com/business/commentary/article-the-last-barrel-of-oil-should-be-a-canadian-one/|title=The last barrel of oil should be a Canadian one|date=2022-10-27|author=Brian Porter|passage=We have forgotten that such a transition will require compromise, as we address real energy needs today, and investment, as we adapt to cleaner ways of producing energy tomorrow. A well-managed transition will '''see''' that the opportunities flowing from the transformation dramatically exceed these costs.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[wait upon]]; [[attend]], [[escort]].
#: {{ux|en|I '''saw''' the old lady safely across the road.}}
#: {{ux|en|You can '''see''' yourself out.}}
# {{lb|en|gambling|transitive}} To respond to another player's [[bet]] with a bet of equal value.
#: {{ux|en|I'll '''see''' your twenty dollars and raise you ten.}}
# To [[determine]] by [[trial]] or [[experiment]]; to [[find out]] (''if'' or ''whether'').
#: {{ux|en|I'll come over later and '''see''' if I can fix your computer.}}
#: {{ux|en|You think I can't beat you in a race, eh? We'll '''see'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|Look to '''see''' if these jeans still fit you.}}
# {{sid|en|refer to}}{{lb|en|used in the imperative}} To [[reference]] or to [[study]] for further [[detail]]s.
#: {{ux|en|Step 4: In the system, check out the laptop to the student ('''see''': "Logging Resources" in the ''Tutor Manual'').}}
#: {{ux|en|For a complete proof of the Poincaré conjecture, '''see''' Appendix C.}}
# To examine something closely, or to utilize something, often as a temporary alternative.
#: {{ux|en|Can I '''see''' that lighter for a second? Mine just quit working.}}
# To include as one of something's experiences.
#: {{ux|en|The equipment has not '''seen''' usage outside of our projects.}}
#: {{ux|en|I '''saw''' military service in Vietnam.}}
